key_insight: Increasing Reynolds number shifts oil-jet breakup from Rayleigh–Plateau instability toward Kelvin–Helmholtz shear-layer breakup, while turbulent dissipation and droplet coalescence jointly shape droplet sizes.
engineering_relevance: Improved droplet-size predictions can inform oil-spill response and liquid–liquid extraction process design.
method: Simultaneous PIV and PLIF measurements of silicone oil injected into refractive-index-matched sugar water.
POD analysis of instability modes and CNN-based segmentation of droplet images.
Population balance modelling extended to include droplet coalescence.
evidence_signal: Measurements show transitional bimodal droplet-size distributions becoming single-peaked at higher Reynolds numbers; including coalescence improves model agreement, especially for larger droplets.
watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative prediction errors or validation beyond the tested fluid system, leaving broader applicability uncertain.
paper_title: Submerged Immiscible Oil Jet: Breakup Dynamics and Droplet Size Modelling
